final_candidates.decision_summary: Conserved glycine providing backbone flexibility in the catalytic core; Gly->Arg introduces a bulky charged sidechain likely to sterically and electrostatically disrupt catalysis. WT Gly at 149 verified.

R157 lies in the N-terminal catalytic FAD-binding region where severe MTHFR-deficiency mutations cluster; losing a conserved Arg salt bridge is likely destabilizing/inactivating. WT Arg at 157 verified.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is stable and no evidence tools are available to refine further.

history.rationale: R157 in the RGDP region is a conserved charged residue likely involved in folate/FAD binding; loss of positive charge often severely reduces MTHFR activity (analogous to known clinical LOF variants).

R157 lies in the catalytic FAD-binding domain; the well-known A222V and severe MTHFR-deficiency mutations cluster in this N-terminal catalytic region, and losing a conserved Arg salt bridge is likely destabilizing/inactivating.
Conserved glycine in a tight-turn (ALRGDP) region; substituting a bulky charged arginine likely introduces steric/backbone strain that disrupts the catalytic fold.

Conserved glycines often provide backbone flexibility at tight turns; a Gly->Arg introduces a bulky charged sidechain likely to sterically/electrostatically disrupt the catalytic core, making LOF probable.
Proline in a conserved segment of the C-terminal regulatory domain; substitution may destabilize the regulatory fold, indirectly compromising function/stability.
Position 572 lies in the C-terminal regulatory (SAM-binding) domain; mutations there tend to alter allosteric regulation rather than abolish catalytic activity, so it is a weaker LOF candidate.

rejection.reason: Position 572 lies in the C-terminal regulatory (SAM-binding) domain; mutations there tend to alter allosteric regulation rather than abolish catalytic activity, so it is a weaker LOF candidate.

history.rationale: Cysteine in the TCCRQR cluster may contribute to structural/catalytic integrity; a large aromatic substitution could disrupt local packing and reduce activity.
C130 sits in the catalytic domain near the CCRQR motif; a Cys->Tyr bulky substitution could disrupt local packing/redox and impair activity, retained as a mid-tier candidate.
